content.summary_of_the_paper: The paper proposes a new architecture inspired by MLPs and transformers for image classification. It revisits the way of doing channel and spatial communication this with convolution. The contributions are as follows: a) Applying 1D depthwise convolution for channel and spatial communication b) Study of the channels splitting c) some theoretical analyses.The method is evaluated on different image classification dataset.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:

- The method is clearly present 
- The paper is quite well written and easy to follow. 
- The paper proposes an evaluation on different datasets which is a good practice.
- The proposed ablations are interesting

Weakness:


- Comparison: 
a) State of the art: The paper state *"Comparison with state of the art. Table 1"* according to the results Table 1 in the paper [1] (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2105.12723v4.pdf) the results here does not seem to be state of the art. It would be interesting to add comparisons with the proposed models Table 1 in the paper [1]

[1] Zhang et al.,  Nested Hierarchical Transformer: Towards Accurate, Data-Efficient and Interpretable Visual Understanding, AAAI 

b) Training:"*Table 1 shows a comparison of SplitMixer with models from MLP, Transformer, and CNN families. Some results are borrowed from Lv et al. (2022) where they trained the models for 200 epochs, whereas here we trained our models for 100 epochs. While
the experimental conditions in Lv et al. (2022) might not be exactly the same as ours, crossexamination still provides insights into how our models fare compared to others, in particular the MLP-based models."*
Training has a significant impact on model performance. In order to have the most accurate comparison it is important to have similar training between the different approaches.

c) ResNet-152 results (79.64 with 150 epochs) Table 2 seems quite low. Indeed in  Wightman et al [1] they reach 80.6 with only 100 epochs (see Table 3, A3 training). 

[1] Wightman et al., ResNet strikes back: An improved training procedure in timm
- Datasets: The results on larger scale datasets with higher resolution images like imageNet-1k seem to be quite bad. Indeed, the proposed method seems to have a lower performance than competing approaches.

- standard deviation:  There is no standard deviation reported which would be useful to better interpret the significance of the results.

- bibliography: the proposed approach seem very close to the  PatchConvnet[1] architecture. Indeed, according to the figure 3 in this paper it seems they have a network with the same MBconv block. It might be interesting to discuss the differences with this paper. In the ResMLP paper (Touvron et al., 2021a)  Table 3 there is an extensive ablation on the patch communication. The positioning of the proposed method must be clarified.
[1] Touvron et al., Augmenting Convolutional networks with attention-based aggregation
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
The paper state: *"In summary, our main contributions are as follows: a) Applying 1D depthwise convolution sequentially across width and height for spatial mixing. We are inspired by the extensive use of spatial
separable convolutions and depthwise separable convolutions in the literature (e.g. MobileNet), b)
Splitting the channels into overlapping or non-overlapping segments and applying 1 × 1 pointwise
convolution to segments for channel mixing, c) Theoretical analyses and empirical support for
computational efficiency of the proposed solution, as well as measuring model throughput, and d)
Ablation analyses to determine the contribution of different model components."*
The contribution seems here rather limited indeed several papers have already studied the way to make the communication between patches with overlap or not. For instance, the proposed approach seem very close to the  PatchConvnet[1] architecture. Indeed, according to the figure 3 in this paper it seems they have a network with the same MBconv block. It might be interesting to discuss the differences with this paper. In the ResMLP paper (Touvron et al., 2021a)  Table 3 there is an extensive ablation on the patch communication. The positioning of the proposed method must be clarified.

The results do not seem very convincing as detailed above. Indeed, the proposed method does not seem to be close to the state of the art on large scale datasets but also on more low scale datasets like CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100.
content.summary_of_the_review: As detailed above, the methodological contribution as well as the results of the proposed method seems insufficient.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This work introduced a lightweight MLP-like architecture, where two depthwise 1D convolutions and grouped pointwise convolutions are used for token mixing and channel mixing, respectively. Besides, four kinds of convolution variants are studied for channel mixing. Experiments are conducted on five image datasets.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength

+: The proposed method is clearly described, and it is easy to implement.

+: Experiments are conducted on various kinds of image classification datasets.


Weaknesses

-: The technical contribution seems incremental. The depthwise 1D convolution and grouped pointwise convolutions are off-the-shelf. The idea on handling height and width of features separately for token mixing appeared in sparse MLP [r1]. Besides, the proposed method seems more engineering, lacking some insights or theoretical analysis on why the proposed method is necessary and can work well. 

[r1] Sparse MLP for Image Recognition: Is Self-Attention Really Necessary? AAAI, 2022.  

-: The experimental results are not convincing.

(1) On Food-101 (Table 1), the proposed method is inferior to ConvMixer and MDMLP.

(2) On ImageNet-1K (Table 2), the proposed SplitMixer-I-1536/20 is inferior to ConvMixer-768/32, which share similar model complexity.

(3) CIFAR is small-scale dataset and easy overfitting. It would better to do ablation study on ImageNet, especially for design of deep architectures.

(4) The running time is very imponent metric for evaluating model complexity, especially for lightweight architectures. The authors would better compare existing methods in terms of running time.

(5) As a new architecture, the authors would better design more variants with different model sizes.

(6) More analysis on results about different kinds of convolution variants for channel mixing seem necessary. 
 
-: The presentation could be further polished. The current version lacks some insights and detailed analysis on the proposed method and looks like a lab report.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: More insights and detailed analysis on the proposed method are necessary, and presentation could be further polished. The proposed method with off-the-shelf techniques seems more engineering, whose technical contribution seems incremental.
content.summary_of_the_review: This work introduced a lightweight MLP-like architecture, which is easy to implement by using standard techniques. The technical contribution of this work seems incremental, and experimental results are not convincing. Besides, the presentation could be further polished.
content.correctness: 2: Several of the paper’s claims are incorrect or not well-supported.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.

content.confidence: 4: You are confident in your assessment, but not absolutely certain. It is unlikely, but not impossible, that you did not understand some parts of the submission or that you are unfamiliar with some pieces of related work.
content.summary_of_the_paper: This work proposes a simple and lightweight MLP-like architecture, named SplitMixer. SplitMixer uses 1D convolutions for spatial mixing and splits the channels into several segments for channel mixing. Extensive experiments on various datasets such as cifar10, cifar100, and imagenet-1k show the effectiveness of the proposed method. It allows sacrificing a small amount of accuracy to achieve the reduction of parameters and flops.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Pros:

(1)  The authors propose a SplitMixer, which is an MLP-like architecture.

(2)  The authors split channels into several segments for channel mixing, which reduces the parameters and flops effectively. 

(3) Extensive experiments on several datasets show the effectiveness of the proposed method.

Cons:
This work aims to design an MLP-like architecture for visual recognition and proposes to split channels to reduce the parameters and flops. I have some questions and concerns. 

(1) It seems that the authors do not carefully evaluate the design of the architecture. The spatial mixing in Figure 1 uses a 1xk depthwise convolution and a kx1 depthwise convolution. However, why do you design it in a cascaded way instead of a parallel way? Does the order of depthwise convolutions affect the final result? Although the main idea of this work is to split channels, spatial mixing, as part of the proposed SplitMixer architecture, is also evaluated. 

(2) In Sec. 2.2, the authors argue that most of the parameters are used for channel mixing. However, it should be better if the authors can provide the specific parameters of spatial mixing and channel mixing. From this formulation, channel mixing uses more parameters than spatial mixing but it is only limited to the case of one-layer operation. I do not know the specific architecture configuration. Thus, the authors can perform a thorough parameter comparison for spatial mixing and channel mixing.

(3) In Table 1, the proposed SplitMixer outperforms most MLP-like architectures with fewer parameters and flops but the results are not superior in Table 2. We know that transformer (e.g., ViT) achieves better performance compared to CNNs when a large amount of data is given [1]. Therefore, can I think that SplitMixer performs better than other methods on small datasets, but fails on large datasets?

(4) The performance of other MLP-like architectures is missing in Table 2. Besides, the throughput of other MLP-like architectures should also be provided for comparisons in Table (5) Some minor points. Table 3 shows CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-10 ablations. It might be CIFAR-100. Some datasets descriptions should be listed in the main text or appendix. 

[1] An Image is Worth 16x16 Words: Transformers for Image Recognition at Scale, in ICLR2021.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: This work has a middle quality and high clarity. According to my knowledge, this work has originality in the split of channels for MLP-like architecture. The results should be reproducible because the authors provide part of the code in Appendix.
content.summary_of_the_review: To sum up, the work proposes a new MLP-like architecture that achieves better results on cifar10 and cifar100 with fewer parameters and flops. However, the results on imagenet-1k are not superior and the performance of some other methods is missing. Some experiments for ablation studies should also be conducted. Therefore, I tend to vote marginally below the acceptance threshold currently.
content.correctness: 3: Some of the paper’s claims have minor issues. A few statements are not well-supported, or require small changes to be made correct.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 3: The contributions are significant and somewhat new. Aspects of the contributions exist in prior work.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes an MLP-like architecture for image classification. Unlike the prior work (ConvMixer, MLPMixer), it relies on 1D depthwise convolutions for spatial and features channel mixing. The motivation behind the proposed mixer is to reduce the number of network parameters thanks to the convolution operation. The approach is evaluated on standard image classification datasets and it shows on-par performance with the related work.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength: 
- The paper is well-written and easy to follow. The proposed approach is clearly presented. Moreover, the differences from the prior work are well-discussed.
- The presented evaluation is in-depth for the task of image classification. 
- The idea of using 1D convolutions to drop the model parameters of an MLP mixer is interesting. 

Weaknesses:

-Although the proposed SplitMixer illustrates solid results compared to its counterparts (MLP-Mixer, ConvMixer, ResMLP), the claim of the paper on reducing the number of parameters compared to the prior work is not strong. The number of parameters is still comparable in most cases. 
- The paper ignores comparisons with recent approaches such as the PoolFormer (CVPR 2022) or When Shift Operation Meets Vision Transformer (IJCAI 2022). These approaches are also aiming to have lightweight models.
- A study of some downstream tasks like object detection could be beneficial to understand the advantages of the proposed method.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
Quality & Clarity:
The paper is well-written and easy to follow. It claims are discusssed into details. At last, the proposed idea is not particularly novel, but it works well in practice.

Reproducibility:
It is relatively easy to reimplement the method. There is source code in the form of text.
content.summary_of_the_review: The paper presents a simple idea to make a mixer-like architecture faster with good performance on image recognition. In general, the paper is well-written and the idea is easy to follow. The major limitation is the lack of comparison with recent transformer architectures. A more detailed evaluation could relate work that is also computed efficiently.
content.correctness: 4: All of the claims and statements are well-supported and correct.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.
